name: Salt of Aspartame-Acesulfame
aliases: E962, INS 962, salt of aspartame-acesulfame, aspartame-acesulfame salt, aspartame acesulfame salt, acesulfame-aspartame salt
what_is: A high-intensity sweetener formed from aspartame and acesulfame, authorised in the EU under E962.
why_botia: This ingredient is actually two sweeteners joined together: aspartame and acesulfame K. Because of the aspartame, the label must warn that it contains phenylalanine — important for people with phenylketonuria. JECFA applies the limits of each of its two components, rather than a separate limit of its own.
can_1: Detect E962 and common forms of the name salt of aspartame-acesulfame.
can_2: Distinguish an E962 declaration from separate declarations of aspartame (E951) and acesulfame K (E950).
cannot_1: Determine the amount of each constituent sweetener from the ingredient list.
cannot_2: Predict an individual's response or phenylalanine intake without quantitative product information.

sources.label: Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008 — E962 in the Union list — consolidated 18 August 2026
